intro.title: Why Mobile-Friendly Design Matters
paragraphs: More than half of all web traffic now comes from smartphones, and for many local and retail businesses it is far higher. Google also uses the mobile version of your site for indexing and ranking. If your website is hard to read, slow or awkward to use on a phone, visitors leave within seconds and your rankings suffer.

Mobile-first web design starts with the smallest screen and builds up. We plan what a phone user needs most, design clear navigation and thumb-friendly buttons, keep pages light and fast, and make calling, messaging on WhatsApp or buying possible in a tap. The same design then adapts responsively to tablets, laptops and large desktop screens.

Whether you need a brand-new mobile-first website, want to convert a non-responsive site into a responsive one, or need UI/UX design for a mobile web app or ecommerce store, our designers handle it end to end. See our <wd>web design services</wd>, read about <redesign>website redesign</redesign> or <contact>get a free mobile audit of your site</contact>.

faqs.title: Mobile Website Design FAQs
faqs.subtitle: Quick answers about mobile-friendly and responsive web design.

items.a: Mobile-first web design means designing a website for phones first and then adapting it for larger screens. It keeps content focused, navigation simple and pages fast, which improves the experience for the majority of visitors who browse on a phone.

items.q: What is the difference between responsive, adaptive and mobile-first design?
items.a: Responsive design uses fluid layouts that adjust to any screen. Adaptive design serves set layouts for specific screen sizes. Mobile-first is an approach where you design for phones first, usually combined with responsive design.

items.q: Can you make my existing website mobile-friendly?
items.a: Yes. We can convert a non-responsive website into a mobile-friendly, responsive one while keeping your content, domain and search rankings, or recommend a redesign if the old site is too limited.

items.q: Why does a mobile-friendly website matter for SEO?
items.a: Google primarily uses the mobile version of your site for indexing and ranking. A fast, mobile-friendly website with good Core Web Vitals is more likely to rank well and keep visitors engaged.

items.q: Do you also design mobile app UI/UX?
items.a: Yes. We design mobile app screens and user flows for Android and iOS, including home screens, ecommerce, booking and payment flows, with clickable prototypes and developer-ready designs.

items.q: How much does mobile website design cost?
items.a: Making an existing site responsive typically costs $300 to $1,000, a new mobile-first website $800 to $3,000, and mobile UI/UX design for apps or ecommerce $1,500 to $6,000.
